request.spec:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A crew is now also a pool: it appears among the pools under its name, with the lead and the
members as its members at equal shares (100.00 split as patrons' shares are, the remainder on the
lead), and receives cuts like any pool. A pool cannot be added with a crew's name nor a crew with a
pool's name. Crew totals stay as they are.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Crews now show up as pools, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass. The front end also type-checks cleanly.

**How it works:** each crew is added to the pools list when that list is loaded, from the crew's current data. Nothing new is written to the database. Each crew appears after the ordinary pools, under its own name. The lead comes first, then the members, each with an equal share of 100.00 split the way patrons' shares are, with the remainder on the lead (three people get 33.34, 33.33 and 33.33). A crew pool then gets its cut of the pot exactly like any other pool, so holds and retirements are handled the same way. Because of this, the person cut totals, the sheet's cut total and the pools CSV export include crews automatically. Crew totals are unchanged.

**Name clashes:** adding a pool with an existing crew's name is refused, and so is adding a crew with an existing pool's name. Both show the form's usual error and write nothing to the store or the audit file.

**Changes:**
- `pool/RespondWithPools.java` builds the crew pools.
- `pool/PoolResponse.java` gets a new `crew` flag. A crew pool's id is the crew's id made negative, so it never collides with a real pool's id.
- `pool/ValidatePool.java` and `crew/ValidateCrew.java` do the name checks.
- On screen, a crew pool has no "add member" form, and it isn't offered as `pool:<name>` when adding a member to another pool. Its members come only from the crew.
- Adding a crew or a crew member now refreshes the pools list.

**Limitation:** a crew pool can't be made a member of another pool. Its members also can't have the from/to dates that ordinary pool members can. The request didn't ask for either, and supporting them would mean storing crew pools as real pool rows instead of building them when the list loads.
